title: Abu Bakr's collection
hookLine: after many memorizers die in battle, Zayd ibn Thabit gathers it into one copy

lines: IF WE LOSE HER, WE LOSE IT.
cards: Think of a family recipe that lives in one grandmother's head. There are notes on the backs of old envelopes, but she's the one who really knows it. Then one winter the family realizes: if we lose her, we lose it.
Somebody has to sit down and gather it before it's too late. Now picture that fear across a whole community, about a book they believe is the word of God.

teach.b: In 632 the Prophet ﷺ died, and Abu Bakr became the first caliph. Within about a year the Muslims fought a hard battle at a place called Yamamah, and many who knew the Qur'an by heart were killed.

teach.h: HOW CAN WE DO WHAT HE DID NOT?
teach.b: Zayd ibn Thabit tells what happened next, in a report in Bukhari. Umar came to Abu Bakr, alarmed: if more memorizers fall, much of the Qur'an could be lost; it should be collected. Abu Bakr hesitated.
How can we do something the Messenger of God did not do? Umar kept urging until, Abu Bakr said, God opened his heart to it.
Then they sent for Zayd: young, trusted, and one of those who had written the revelation for the Prophet. His reply is one of the most human lines in the story.
By God, if they had asked me to move a mountain, it would not have been heavier. But he did it. He searched it out from the same places as yesterday: palm stalks, flat stones and the chests of men.
Other reports say he accepted no written piece unless witnesses confirmed it. He tells us he found the closing verses of the ninth surah written with only one man, Abu Khuzaymah al-Ansari.
The result was a set of sheets, gathered in one place. They stayed with Abu Bakr until he died, then with Umar, then with Umar's daughter Hafsah, one of the Prophet's widows.
And Muslims say what this collection was not: new words, or an edit. It was the same Qur'an already recited and written, brought from many places into one.

how: Muslims teach the collection under Abu Bakr as the moment the Qur'an's written pieces and memorizers were brought together into one set of sheets, and remember Zayd ibn Thabit as the companion who carried it out.

games.q: you're Zayd ibn Thabit. the caliph asks you to gather the whole Qur'an into one copy. what do you say?
o: moving a mountain would be lighter.
games.why: Zayd said moving a mountain would not have been heavier, and then he did it anyway.

practice: Bring one scattered thing together in your mind: the loose papers on a table, the photos of someone you love spread across three devices, the verses you've learned this year. Name the pieces, and where each one is.
If you pray, you can thank Allah for the people who kept what mattered.

wordCard.voice: Zayd. The young scribe Abu Bakr and Umar sent to gather the scattered Qur'an into one set of sheets.
